chapter: Callers: Papa John Joseph to Congo Square
title: 'Congo Square' and the mood Wiggs intended
summary: Wiggs says he composed 'Congo Square' to evoke slaves singing there.

bands.name: Johnny Wiggs and His New Orleans Kings

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This is WTIS 690 in New Orleans, Louisiana, and you are listening to Let's Talk It Over with your moderator, Joseph Collada.

Okay, back in tune with more of Let's Talk It Over. We have, well, not a lot of time to play all of the records that Dick Allen had selected this morning. I knew this was going to happen. I asked them to choose some. I'm going to ask if we can jump over Snoozer Quinn now. I want to go back to Johnny Wiggs and the New Orleans Kings, because this is a great song. Congo Square. You know, that has a bit of a tear in it. I can picture somebody sitting around the waterfront at about 3 o'clock on a Sunday morning, you know, 3 a.m., with that in the background. Is that what you meant, Mr. Wiggins?

Well, you know, we all have metal pictures of music. Actually, what I had in mind when I put that thing on paper was to give a bit of the color, which I supposed imagined took place in Congo Square when the people used to permit the slaves to go out and sing their beautiful slave songs in Congo Square. And I tried to think up an atmosphere which would sort of go along with that.
